findings.reason: the followup's pass and job counts must match the section it wires, or the node that builds §34 measures half the matrix the section's done-when closes on.
findings.text: the open followup f-araiid-025, the dispatch wiring for §33 and §34, says "§34 re-measures the bounds live, with five passes per arm, one job per arm"; under the plan's own convention arm means storage (§20 "five timed passes per arm"), so the wiring reads as five passes per storage, while §34's title and Deliverable now require five passes per revision on each storage, ten per storage — a coordinator dispatching §34 from the followup would specify half the passes the section demands and report n=5 as complete

findings.reason: a tolerance the plan's own cited noise measurement contradicts turns the section's instrument check into a re-run loop instead of the before-to-after discrimination the bound needs.
findings.text: §34's A/A check "passes when the median of a revision's first two passes and the median of its last two agree within 15 percent", but §24's own report (the evidence §34's Why cites) records identical arms disagreeing by up to 51.6 percent and a single arm's own two passes at 226.447 s and 125.460 s, and §24 failed the same 15 percent A/A it declared; on that evidence a 15 percent in-job tolerance has no support, and §§34's failure path is "the job is re-run", so each re-run costs about a fence and the section may never produce the bound verdict it exists to give

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — §34's citations to §21, §24 and §33 all resolve; §33 precedes §34, and §24's harness, corpus and run r-20261018T020037545719 resolve to the report at the-repaired-pass-is-measured-against-the-freshness-window/report.md.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §34's in-job A/A check fixes a 15 percent agreement the plan's own §24 evidence (up to 51.6 percent disagreement) shows is unreachable at this scale, and its failure path is a re-run, so the bound verdict is likely never produced.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — "Write path: the run's report directory" is durable, matching §24's own report location.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §34 introduces no code symbols or comments; the identifiers it names (`fleet_state`, `sweep`, `_run_file_record`, `copy.deepcopy`, `posix.stat`) are mechanism names, and the run id it would carry is emitted data like a checkpoint path.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated cause (§24 could not buy five passes inside one 60-minute fence) is what §24's report shows, and the split into one job per storage with an in-job A/A is capable of producing the done-when's five-pass medians.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §34 carries one deliverable, the re-measurement of the bounded pass against the freshness window, with no product change.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — the open followup f-araiid-025, which is the dispatch wiring for §33→§34, states §34's measure as "five passes per arm, one job per arm", but §34 now requires five passes per *revision* on each storage (ten passes per storage).
